Theme

Nature & food · Household, washing & chores

dung noun

also manure, droppings, muck, dunghill, fertiliser, fertilizer, compost

classical

Verg. G. 1.80 (Lewis & Short)
Plin. NH 28.234 (Lewis & Short)

fimus, fimī m.

noun, second declension

dung, manure

Also neuter, fimum (Pliny).

Other words

  • stercus, stercoris n. — dung, droppings, muck

    noun, third declension · classical · Cato Agr. 29 (Lewis & Short); Varr. RR 1.38 (Lewis & Short); Col. 2.15 (Lewis & Short)

    The farm writers’ word for manure.

  • laetāmen, laetāminis n. — manure

    noun, third declension · also used · post-classical · Plin. NH 18.141 (Lewis & Short)

    From laetus in its farm sense, rich, fertile: what makes the soil rich.

Examples

  • ārida tantum nē saturāre fimō pinguī pudeat sola

    only do not be ashamed to drench dry soil with rich dungVerg. G. 1.79–80

See also garden, grow, cow, trail, manure.

SourcesLewis & Short: fimus · Lewis & Short: stercus · Lewis & Short: laetamen

Vergil, Georgica 1.79–80.
